set.body:
Source: architecture review of modules/multivar, verified against the code on 2026-07-08 (every claim checked; all held).

Problem: the duality-diagram spine (X, D, Q) is the correct unifying substrate and is load-bearing for single-table methods (GenPCA/PCA/CPCA), but decorative for the rest. Paired methods (PLSC/CCA/RRR) build a PairedDualityDiagram only for shape validation, then compute unweighted X'Y; CPCA speaks a second projection dialect on raw matrices; PCA has ~4 parallel routines; fit results carry an overloaded, untyped singularValues slot with throwing accessors. It is one elegant core with partially-redundant satellites.

Keystone: two-table methods are the SVD of a shared-row-metric cross-operator Q_X^{1/2} X'D Y Q_Y^{1/2} — PLSC=(I,I), CCA=(Sxx^-1,Syy^-1), RRR=asymmetric — exactly as single-table methods are eigendecompositions of XQX'D. Routing the paired estimators through it makes D-weighting free, regularization a metric, and deletes three bespoke numeric paths. That is the single highest-leverage change.

Recommended sequence (risk-ordered — cheap type-safety wins first, deep numeric refactor last):
  0. Build R-parity fixtures for PLSC/CCA/RRR  [precondition for the keystone]
  1. Unify the fit result (discriminated Spectrum)
  2. Collapse the CPCA constraint triple-encoding
  3. Narrow PairedLatentMethod
  4. Single PCA path (Pca = GenPca identity backend)   [after 1]
  5. One projection contract (MvMap, not MatrixMap)
  6. KEYSTONE: crossGram / PairedGmd                     [after 0; sequence after 1 and 5]
  7. Bridge (not merge) RowGeometry

Honest caveats: (a) the keystone rewrites exactly the code that has no R-parity oracle today, so item 0 is a hard precondition; (b) the win is cohesion + free D-weighting + path deletion, not speed — CCA still forms and inverts the column Gram. RowGeometry stays a separate geometry by design.

This epic is done when all child items are closed.
set.title: EPIC: multivar — unify the method algebra on the duality-diagram spine
